title: Moderate Weakness. No New Reasons
summary:
Moderate Weakness. No New Reasons 

             
             
            Bonds lost ground on Friday, but not for any new, overt reasons. At times, weakness coincided with higher oil prices, but we don't love that explanation considering oil was higher on Monday when yields were substantially lower. PPI data is also not a compelling market mover as it came in right in line with forecasts and doesn't look like it will pass much through to core PCE. Given that short term yields rallied (2yr still down 2bps), much of today's volatility could simply be explained by curve trading amid lighter liquidity. In the bigger picture, the decisive selling pressure of the past 2 sessions basically leveled off and now we wait for the next shoe to drop.

title: Mortgage Rates Have Given Back Almost All of October's Gains
summary: In 3 short days, the average top tier 30yr fixed mortgage rate has risen 0.32% to 7.50%, erasing a vast majority of the improvement seen over the past 5 weeks. Today's increase wasn't nearly as sharp as each of the previous 2 days, but it wasn't small either.  Notably, rates went higher today even though the underlying bond market held reasonably steady. On most days, a flat bond market would result in far less rate movement. Today was an exception largely due to timing. Yesterday afternoon saw bonds lose ground late in the day--too late for the average lender to go to the trouble of changing their rates to reflect the shift in the underlying market.   This happens occasionally and, when it does, lenders simply account for the late-day market movement in the following morning's rate offerings. In addition, lenders can also set rates a bit more conservatively on Fridays.

title: Existing-Home Sales Sink to Lowest Level Since 2010
summary:
Existing-home sales had another rough month, and just hit their lowest level since August 2010. Mortgage rates are largely to blame.  The National Association of REALTORS® (NAR) reported a  5.5% monthly decline  and an  8.8% year-over-year decline , bringing the seasonally adjusted annual sales rate to just  3.75 million . Chief Economist Lawrence Yun attributed the weakness to mortgage rates, which have tested levels not seen since 2000.    Inventory continued to improve modestly, even as sales slowed. Total housing inventory reached  1.59 million units , up 1.3% from September and  4.6% year over year,  a  5.1-month supply.  Homes also took slightly longer to sell, with the median time on market increasing to  35 days  from 33 days in September.  Prices continued to rise nationally, although at a much slower pace. Median prices crawled to  $416,700 , up a mere  0.4% from October 2025 . Still, that marked the  40th consecutive month  of year-over-year price gains. The Housing Affordability Index fell to  100.7 , down from 107.3 a year earlier, with affordability deteriorating across the country.   Regional Breakdown (Sales and Prices, October 2026)

title: Decent Bounce in Mortgage Demand Thanks to Last Week's Lower Rates
summary: Mortgage applications bounced back in the latest week, with both purchase and refinance activity moving higher. The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) reported a  6.2% increase  in total application volume for the week ending November 6, 2026.  NOTE: That Nov 6th date is important as it marked the bottom of the range for interest rates after a nice decline that began in mid October. Rates have risen sharply since then so all that follows is likely a bit of a retrospective. In other words, application demand will probably fall again in next week's data thanks to this week's higher rates.   Purchase applications led the improvement, rising 8% on a seasonally adjusted basis, while refinances increased 5%. Despite the weekly gains, both categories remain well below year-ago levels.      Purchase applications were still  18% below year-ago levels , while refinance activity was down  57% . The refinance share of total applications held steady at 39.8%, while adjustable-rate mortgage applications accounted for 10.9% of activity, down slightly from the previous week.  “The declining trend in rates helped to spur stronger application activity, although the pace of purchase and refinance applications remain considerably lower than a year ago,” said MBA's Joel Kan. FHA and VA purchase applications saw particularly strong gains. The FHA rate fell below 7% for the first time in several weeks, reaching 6.98%, more than 20 basis points below the conforming rate. It is important to note: Kan references the Freddie Mac rate survey here, and real rates have risen materially in the past few days.

title: Nearly Unchanged After As-Expected PPI
summary: This morning's Producer Price Index (PPI) came out as expected. The components that impact core PCE were also uneventful. Stocks and bonds initially rallied but the gains were erased in less than 20 minutes. Higher oil prices coincided with the bounce toward higher yields, but the longer-term correlation remains weak enough that we wouldn't read too much into that. After 9:30am, stocks are selling off enough to bring bond yields just a hair lower from intraday highs. All-in-all, we suspect the modest weakness in 10yr Treasuries is best viewed through the lens of traders squaring yesterday's curve trading positions amid lighter mid-November liquidity.  5yr yields just hit 'unchanged' levels and MBS are close to doing the same.

title: House Passes Bill To Nearly Triple VA Streamline Refinance Fee
summary: Legislation that would nearly triple the funding fee on VA streamline refinances cleared the House on Veterans Day, reviving a proposal that drew objections from the mortgage industry earlier this year.The Take Care of America's Veterans Act, passed Wednesday, Nov. 11, would increase the funding fee on VA Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loans (IRRRLs) from 0.5% to 1.42%. It would also double the fee for assuming an existing VA-backed mortgage from 0.5% to 1%.
